networks.name: Chebucto Community Net
networks.context: A community-run doorway to email, information and the early web in Halifax.
history: Organizers began meeting at the Halifax Library.

networks.name: Vancouver Community Network
networks.context: Vancouver FreeNet evolved into VCN, preserving a community focus through the move from dial-up to the web.
history: The organization began as Vancouver FreeNet.
By this year VCN had moved to a web-based information system and offered community web hosting.

networks.name: National Capital FreeNet
networks.context: A Carleton University organizing project became a public community network in the national capital.
history: The organizing project began at Carleton University.
Donated modems and communications equipment connected the Ottawa Public Library.
The public opening took place at the regional headquarters in Ottawa.

networks.name: Victoria Free-Net
networks.context: The 1995 Canadian community-network directory documents public dial-up, telnet, gopher and web addresses in Victoria.
history: Listed in the Canadian Community Networks Directory with a web address at freenet.victoria.bc.ca/vifa.html.

networks.name: Toronto Free-Net
networks.context: The contemporary directory records donated equipment, institutional support and thousands of activated accounts.
history: Operational by this date, according to the 1995 Canadian Community Networks Directory.
The directory records approximately 14,000 activated accounts by this date.

networks.name: Sympatico
networks.context: A commercial counterpart to the FreeNets: an ISP portal combining access, email, news and web directories. This collection stops at 2005 to focus on its early era.
history: Bell launched Sympatico.MSN.ca with Microsoft, combining the two portals, according to BCE’s 2005 annual filing.

networks.name: Shaw / Shaw @Home era
networks.context: Explore the early cable-internet era through Shaw’s archived homepages. A company homepage is not proof that a particular product was offered on that capture date. This collection stops at 2001.
history: Shaw says it launched high-speed Internet service in Calgary on this date.
A CRTC hearing described Shaw @Home as the Shaw-branded @Home service.
